Synopsis:
The player talks to Wyll on their second night at camp.

Cluster Contexts:
- CAMP_Night2_CRD_Wyll.json: You're at your camp on the party's second night together; Wyll is a companion who sits down for a private camp conversation. Off‑screen the group has been through frightening encounters recently (monsters, screams, undead and other dangers), which Wyll uses as examples to make a larger point about fear. The player replies with light, slightly risqué banter and Wyll briefly hem‑hawes, then shifts to an earnest, inspirational bit about doubt being the worst enemy and the need to press on. This is a personal morale moment — other companions might be nearby, but the exchange is meant to reassure and rally the player.
- Wyll_Recruitment_PostDruidAttack_PostEA.json: Post EADialogue with Wyll after Druid Attack. In most cases, this will involve him training a tiefling child before the player breaks in, and you discover you were both on the mind flayer ship. Wyll comes across as a big-time hero, and wants help killing goblins. He is called the Blade of Frontiers by most.
- Wyll_Recruitment_PostEA.json: Post EA dialog version.Initial dialogue with Wyll. In most cases, this will involve him training a tiefling child before the player breaks in, and you discover you were both on the mind flayer ship. Wyll comes across as a big-time hero, and wants help killing goblins. He is called the Blade of Frontiers by most.
- PB_Astarion_Wyll_Gale_Cazador.json: Astarion asks Wyll if he knows the vampire Cazador. Wyll doesn't, but Gale has read about the Szaar coven. Nasty creatures. Astarion quietly agrees.
- SCL_Drider_Caravan_HalfOrcCaster.json: You’ve just cleared a checkpoint and entered a cultist camp in the Shadow‑cursed lands, where Kansif (a stoic, honourable half‑orc) and Brawler Vez (a mouthy goblin) are on watch. Absolute cultists here expect a “True Soul” sent by Nightwarden Minthara who will carry a spider‑lyre used to call a drider guide; cult guards commonly perform telepathic checks for tadpoles, and a positive reading will mark you as a True Soul and change how they treat you. If you actually possess the lyre you can play it to summon the drider (who may answer with worshipful voices like Kar’niss’s); if not, the cultists will offer information about where the instrument can be found. In some versions of the scene Harpers and ambushes around Moonrise tie into the encounter, so nearby allies or tension from recent skirmishes can affect how quickly things escalate.

Sample 1:
- Wyll: Question for you: have you ever heard a banshee's scream? (node 20)
- Player: No, but I once made one whimper a bit. (node 21)
- Wyll: Yes, well - ahem. If you'd ever actually heard one, you'd not heard a whimper, but a wail. || [context] NodeContext: Hemming and hawing after a slightly lascivious joke. (node 10)

- Wyll: I thought it the most terrible noise in all sixteen planes. But there's one even more fearsome than that. (node 7)
- Player: The shrieks of the goblins at the grove's gates? (node 16)
- Wyll: They screeched most horribly, yes - but I know of one even more ruthless: (node 18)
- Wyll: The doubt in our minds crying out for attention. (node 26)
- Wyll: 'It's hopeless', it says. 'Stop resisting. Give up and give in.' (node 17)
- Wyll: Doubt is the greatest villain we face. Greater than all the Hells' devils, greater than a murderous god. (node 13)
- Wyll: Most people don't find it so easy to conquer. It's a good thing for us that we aren't 'most people'. (node 2)
- Wyll: Slay your doubt, and nothing can stop you. Not a demon, not a dragon, and certainly not an illithid worm. (node 3)
- Wyll: I'm glad to see you're not one to give up. (node 1)

context: You're on the party's second night at camp and Wyll — a companion who recently joined the group — sits down for a private talk. Off‑screen the party has been through frightening encounters (shrill banshee‑like screams, undead, goblin attacks and other dangers) that Wyll uses as examples to make a larger point about fear. The player replies with light, slightly risqué banter; Wyll briefly hem‑hawes, then shifts into an earnest, rallying speech that calls doubt the worst enemy and urges pressing on. It's meant as a personal morale moment to reassure and inspire the player — other companions may be nearby, but this exchange is intimate.
